To: ashbourne-terrace-chimney
Replying to: p05
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT — please do not enter 43

Mick, please don’t go into 43 at 9, with or without props, and please don’t take your lad in. Priya, please don’t hand over a key for this. No loft inspection from inside either.

I’m a chartered structural engineer with IStructE, but I’m speaking here only as a neighbour who looked from the opposite pavement at about 7. This isn’t a commission or a structural inspection, and I have no professional indemnity cover for informal advice.

Part of 41’s stack is still standing and appears to lean towards 43, with visibly deteriorated mortar at its base. At 43 there’s a substantial hole in the roof, stepped cracking above the bay and apparent movement at the bay head. Loose slates remain above the pavement at 43 and 45.

Standing under that damaged roof to fit props, with loose masonry above, puts you in a particularly dangerous position. Floors may already be carrying fallen debris; we don’t know how loads are now being supported. Two props placed without an assessment could make matters worse. Victorian terraces can be robust, as JoJo’s cousin says, but that doesn’t establish the safety of this damaged terrace.

Priya: I cannot say that Mrs Doherty is safe. Although 45’s frontage looks undamaged, I couldn’t see the shared wall between 43 and 45. It isn’t my decision, but I would not sleep in her front room tonight. Staying with family until 45 has been checked would be the safer course.

The council already knows, but the tape only closes 43’s garden, not the footway. That does not mean the pavement is safe. Please use the opposite side until the council has assessed it, especially on the school run. Contact the council again now about the remaining stack, loose slates and unclosed footway; out-of-hours dangerous structures calls go through the main council number.

---
To: dm:Gary_41
Replying to: d01
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT — urgent information for dangerous structures

Gary, I won’t put your private details on the forum. But please tell the council’s dangerous structures officer about the chimney breast removals and reported supports immediately, before anyone enters. That information matters to their assessment. Don’t go inside to check anything yourself.

I can’t establish the cause from the pavement or advise on insurance. A private conversation with me mustn’t delay getting this information to the officer.
